input.prompt:
READ-ONLY audit of Linear issues. Do NOT change anything in Linear (no save_issue, no comments). Do not run any git commands that change HEAD or branches.

Context: Linear project "Paigasus Helikon" (team SMA), a Rust AI-agent SDK. Load Linear tools with ToolSearch "select:mcp__claude_ai_Linear__get_issue,mcp__claude_ai_Linear__list_comments,mcp__claude_ai_Linear__list_issues".

Label convention (from well-tagged issues like SMA-816, SMA-803): each issue has
- one or more `area:*` labels: area:core, area:providers, area:sessions, area:runtime, area:tools, area:mcp, area:macros, area:evals, area:observability, area:docs, area:ci, area:release, area:deps, area:testing
- one `stage:*` label: stage:0 Foundation (workspace, CI, release, deps); stage:1 single-agent MVP; stage:2 multi-agent+MCP+guardrails; stage:3 production hardening (all current open work is stage:3)
- exactly one type label: Bug, Feature, or Improvement
Priority: 1 Urgent, 2 High, 3 Medium, 4 Low, 0 None.

Issues to audit: SMA-819, SMA-820, SMA-621, SMA-585, SMA-567, SMA-565, SMA-564, SMA-548, SMA-544, SMA-532, SMA-523, SMA-450.

For each issue: call get_issue with includeRelations true; read the description (and comments if they matter for scope). Then propose:
1. The full correct label set.
2. The correct priority, with a one-line reason. Keep the current priority unless there is a clear reason to change it. A fresh issue with "No priority" needs one. Correctness bugs that give wrong output to users rank above test-only or doc-only gaps.
3. Missing blocking relations: if the description or comments say an issue depends on, needs, follows, or must land after another SMA issue (open or done), or one issue's fix is a precondition for another (e.g. SMA-567 extends the conformance suite from SMA-533; SMA-564 vs SMA-567), list it as "X blocks Y". Only list a relation when the text gives evidence; quote the evidence briefly. Note existing relations so they are not duplicated. Ignore relations to issues that are already Done unless the blocked issue is still open AND the blocker is still open — a done blocker needs no relation. Also flag "related" (non-blocking) links only if strongly evident.

Return a compact table: issue | current labels | proposed labels | current prio | proposed prio + reason | blocking relations to add (with evidence). Be terse.

{"id":"SMA-819","uuid":"55003e53-0a09-43fa-9be0-bef2317ecbf4","title":"Anthropic translator sends an empty text block for an empty user text part","description":"The Anthropic chat translator sends `{"type": "text", "text": ""}` when a user message has an empty text part. The Messages API requires non-empty text blocks, so the request probably fails with HTTP 400. Because the message is in the session, each replay of that session repeats the failure.

Two paths cause this:

* An empty user input. This is on `main` before PR #346.
* A turn-boundary checkpoint that returns `Inject([Text ""])` (PR #346).

## Required behavior

* The translator drops text blocks that are empty or contain only whitespace.
* The translator does not send a user message that has no blocks left.
* The rule applies to every message, so replayed session items are also covered.

## Acceptance criteria

* A live check against the Messages API (or a keyless proxy container) confirms the 400 for an empty block and the fix.
* The test `empty_text_part_is_emitted_as_empty_block` in the Anthropic `request.rs` tests changes to assert that the block is dropped.
* New tests cover whitespace-only text and a user message with no remaining blocks.

{"id":"SMA-820","uuid":"c211602b-e548-4b8a-ba1b-1f166d3cd273","title":"Gemini translator sends two adjacent user contents after a tool result","description":"The Gemini translator maps a tool result to a `role: user` content with a `functionResponse` part. When a user message comes directly after the tool result, the translator sends a second `role: user` content. The request then has two `role: user` contents next to each other.

No official source says whether the Gemini API accepts this. If the API rejects it or handles it badly, the run fails at the next model call.

Two paths cause this shape:

* A turn-boundary checkpoint that returns `Inject(..)` after a tool turn (PR #346).
* A resumed run after a deferred tool call. This shape is on `main` before PR #346.

## Required behavior

* The translator merges adjacent contents that have the same role into one content, and keeps the order of the parts.
* The rule applies to every message, so replayed session items are also covered.

## Acceptance criteria

* A live check against the Gemini API (or a keyless proxy container) shows how the API handles two adjacent `role: user` contents, before and after the fix.
* The Gemini `request.rs` test that pins the tool-result-then-user-message shape changes to assert one merged `role: user` content.
* A new test covers a merge of more than two adjacent contents with the same role.","priority":{"value":3,"name":"Medium"},"url":"https://linear.app/smaschek/issue/SMA-820/gemini-translator-sends-two-adjacent-user-contents-after-a-tool-result","gitBranchName":"feature/sma-820-gemini-translator-sends-two-adjacent-user","createdAt":"2026-11-20T13:58:04.469Z","updatedAt":"2026-11-20T14:22:43.679Z","archivedAt":null,"completedAt":null,"startedAt":null,"canceledAt":null,"dueDate":null,"slaStartedAt":null,"slaMediumRiskAt":null,"slaHighRiskAt":null,"slaBreachesAt":null,"status":"Backlog","statusType":"backlog","labels":["area:providers","stage:3","Bug"],"attachments":[],"documents":[],"createdBy":"Sven Maschek","createdById":"ba6021cb-56c5-43aa-9797-fab3599d7ead","project":"Paigasus Helikon","projectId":"5d1fd72d-af2d-40f5-b562-fa04f8018610","team":"Sven Maschek","teamId":"7178572e-d61f-4cf0-bbcb-4e03c8d9f39e"}

{"id":"SMA-621","uuid":"84824b54-31f4-4bcf-9c61-37eebdff0b23","title":"ModelTurnAccumulator merges parallel blank-call_id tool calls, failing the turn on concatenated args","description":"Raised by CodeRabbit on the <issue id="c590d5a2-5978-4bed-bfda-915404efc5d2" label="SMA-619" href="https://linear.app/smaschek/issue/SMA-619/litellm-upgrades-a-blank-call-id-after-emission-splitting-one-call" /> PR (#249, thread [r3948857802](<https://github.com/SMK1085/paigasus-helikon/pull/249#discussion_r3948857802>)) and deferred there as out of scope. <issue id="c590d5a2-5978-4bed-bfda-915404efc5d2" label="SMA-619" href="https://linear.app/smaschek/issue/SMA-619/litellm-upgrades-a-blank-call-id-after-emission-splitting-one-call" /> pinned the cost with a test rather than fixing it; this is the ticket that owns the fix, if we want one.

## The defect

`ModelTurnAccumulator::observe` groups tool-call deltas by `call_id` (`crates/paigasus-helikon-core/src/model.rs:594`) with no exemption for the blank id, joins each group's `args_delta`s into one string, and parses that string exactly once (`model.rs:539-544`). A parse failure propagates out of `finish()` (`model.rs:624`) and discards the **entire turn, assistant text included**.

So N parallel tool calls that all arrive under `call_id: ""` collapse into a single `Item::ToolCall`, first-name-wins, with every call's arguments concatenated:

```text
("", Some("alpha"), "")  ("", Some("beta"), "")
("", None, "{\"p\":1}")  ("", None, "{\"q\":2}")

-> one item, name "alpha", args_str "{\"p\":1}{\"q\":2}" -> Err, whole turn dropped
```

`beta` is lost outright. With no arguments at all the turn survives but still yields one call where the backend sent two.

## This is documented, not accidental

`ModelEvent::ToolCallDelta`'s contract (`model.rs:189-197`, tightened by <issue id="d345d77f-6510-4c89-9aad-3bb196bfcedc" label="SMA-616" href="https://linear.app/smaschek/issue/SMA-616/litellm-flush-buffered-names-drops-a-blank-id-calls-name-via-the-call" />) states the rule and then states that this crate breaks it:

> The non-blank qualifier is deliberate. A backend may send `"id": ""`, and an empty id cannot identify a call — so a provider MUST NOT merge two parallel blank-id calls, and two such calls therefore each carry a name under `""`. Consumers that need one entry per call should key on a non-blank `call_id` and treat `""` as "unidentified". This crate's own `ModelTurnAccumulator` does not follow that advice: it deliberately merges blank-id calls together, first-name-wins, the same as any other `call_id`.

The translators hold up their end — `providers-litellm` and `openai/chat` both emit one name-carrying delta per blank-id call, pinned by `blank_ids_do_not_collapse_distinct_calls` and `blank_ids_do_not_collapse_at_end_of_stream` in each. The gap is entirely between the event layer and the accumulator.

## Why it is more reachable after <issue id="c590d5a2-5978-4bed-bfda-915404efc5d2" label="SMA-619" href="https://linear.app/smaschek/issue/SMA-619/litellm-upgrades-a-blank-call-id-after-emission-splitting-one-call" />

<issue id="c590d5a2-5978-4bed-bfda-915404efc5d2" label="SMA-619" href="https://linear.app/smaschek/issue/SMA-619/litellm-upgrades-a-blank-call-id-after-emission-splitting-one-call" /> stops a blank `call_id` being upgraded to a real one once a delta has already gone out under `""` — otherwise one call splits across two ids and the real one carries no name. Keeping the call under `""` is the right call at the event layer, but it means streams that previously ended up under real ids now stay blank, so **more** streams reach the accumulator merge. <issue id="c590d5a2-5978-4bed-bfda-915404efc5d2" label="SMA-619" href="https://linear.app/smaschek/issue/SMA-619/litellm-upgrades-a-blank-call-id-after-emission-splitting-one-call" /> did not change the accumulator; it widened the input set.

Pinned there by `withheld_upgrades_keep_parallel_blank_calls_merged` (`crates/paigasus-helikon-providers-litellm/src/stream.rs`), which asserts `finish()` returns `Err` and records the trade as accepted. That test is the thing to update if this is fixed.

## Nothing downstream defends against it

There is no validation of a blank `call_id` anywhere in the loop. `build_items` constructs `Item::ToolCall { call_id: "", .. }` unconditionally and defaults a missing name to `""` (`model.rs:545-549`); `loop_state.rs:278-300` dispatches on the presence of an `Item::ToolCall` and matches handoffs by `name` with no check that the call is identifiable. A blank-id call that *does* survive is dispatched as a tool named `""`.

## Options

1. **Exempt the blank id in the accumulator** — give each blank-id delta run its own bucket rather than keying on `""`. Cheapest, and confined to `core`. Needs a rule for what separates two runs, since the only signal is delta ordering.
2. **Surface it as an error** — refuse to build an `Item::ToolCall` with a blank `call_id` and return a `ModelError`/violation instead. Honest, but changes the `ModelEvent` contract and needs every translator moved in lockstep. This is <issue id="c590d5a2-5978-4bed-bfda-915404efc5d2" label="SMA-619" href="https://linear.app/smaschek/issue/SMA-619/litellm-upgrades-a-blank-call-id-after-emission-splitting-one-call" /> spec §2.3's considered-and-rejected alternative, rejected on scope rather than on merit.
3. **Do nothing, document harder.** The current state: accurate docs, a test pinning the cost, and a `warn!` naming each discarded id.

## Scope warning

Whatever is chosen, this is a **cross-provider** change, not a `core`-only one. Six translators carry blank-id handling (`providers-litellm`, `openai/chat`, `openai/responses`, `providers-anthropic`, `providers-bedrock`, `providers-gemini`), and `openai/responses` has no blank-id handling at all — its own name-dedup defect is open as <issue id="3babda5a-6506-488b-aefb-c4dfe16aab1e" label="SMA-617" href="https://linear.app/smaschek/issue/SMA-617/openairesponses-can-emit-two-name-carrying-deltas-for-one-call-id-via" />. `tests/provider-stream-conformance`'s assertion 7 (`src/check.rs`) is deliberately **not** scoped to non-blank ids, and its comment says the first blank-id fixture to arrive will trip it — that is the decision point this ticket would reach.

## Acceptance criteria

* A decision is recorded between options 1-3, with the reasoning, before any code changes.
* If 1 or 2: two parallel blank-id calls carrying distinct arguments survive `ModelTurnAccumulator::finish()` as two items, or fail with a diagnostic that names the ambiguity — not with a `serde_json` trailing-characters error.
* A test drives that shape and is verified to FAIL against `main` first.
* `withheld_upgrades_keep_parallel_blank_calls_merged` and `ModelEvent::ToolCallDelta`'s doc comment are updated to match whatever is decided; neither may be left asserting the old behaviour.
* The conformance suite's assertion 7 is either left unscoped deliberately or scoped with the reasoning recorded in `check.rs`.","priority":{"value":4,"name":"Low"},"url":"https://linear.app/smaschek/issue/SMA-621/modelturnaccumulator-merges-parallel-blank-call-id-tool-calls-failing","gitBranchName":"feature/sma-621-modelturnaccumulator-merges-parallel-blank","createdAt":"2026-09-07T17:56:48.500Z","updatedAt":"2026-11-20T14:22:45.347Z","archivedAt":null,"completedAt":null,"startedAt":null,"canceledAt":null,"dueDate":null,"slaStartedAt":null,"slaMediumRiskAt":null,"slaHighRiskAt":null,"slaBreachesAt":null,"status":"Backlog","statusType":"backlog","labels":["area:providers","area:core","stage:3","Bug"],"attachments":[],"documents":[],"createdBy":"Sven Maschek","createdById":"ba6021cb-56c5-43aa-9797-fab3599d7ead","project":"Paigasus Helikon","projectId":"5d1fd72d-af2d-40f5-b562-fa04f8018610","team":"Sven Maschek","teamId":"7178572e-d61f-4cf0-bbcb-4e03c8d9f39e"}

This is <issue id="c590d5a2-5978-4bed-bfda-915404efc5d2" label="SMA-619" href="https://linear.app/smaschek/issue/SMA-619/litellm-upgrades-a-blank-call-id-after-emission-splitting-one-call" /> spec §2.3's considered-and-rejected alternative, rejected on scope rather than on merit.
3. **Do nothing, document harder.** The current state: accurate docs, a test pinning the cost, and a `warn!` naming each discarded id.

## Scope warning

Whatever is chosen, this is a **cross-provider** change, not a `core`-only one. Six translators carry blank-id handling (`providers-litellm`, `openai/chat`, `openai/responses`, `providers-anthropic`, `providers-bedrock`, `providers-gemini`), and `openai/responses` has no blank-id handling at all — its own name-dedup defect is open as <issue id="3babda5a-6506-488b-aefb-c4dfe16aab1e" label="SMA-617" href="https://linear.app/smaschek/issue/SMA-617/openairesponses-can-emit-two-name-carrying-deltas-for-one-call-id-via" />. `tests/provider-stream-conformance`'s assertion 7 (`src/check.rs`) is deliberately **not** scoped to non-blank ids, and its comment says the first blank-id fixture to arrive will trip it — that is the decision point this ticket would reach.

## Acceptance criteria

* A decision is recorded between options 1-3, with the reasoning, before any code changes.
* If 1 or 2: two parallel blank-id calls carrying distinct arguments survive `ModelTurnAccumulator::finish()` as two items, or fail with a diagnostic that names the ambiguity — not with a `serde_json` trailing-characters error.
* A test drives that shape and is verified to FAIL against `main` first.

* The conformance suite's assertion 7 is either left unscoped deliberately or scoped with the reasoning recorded in `check.rs`.","priority":{"value":4,"name":"Low"},"url":"https://linear.app/smaschek/issue/SMA-621/modelturnaccumulator-merges-parallel-blank-call-id-tool-calls-failing","gitBranchName":"feature/sma-621-modelturnaccumulator-merges-parallel-blank","createdAt":"2026-09-07T17:56:48.500Z","updatedAt":"2026-11-20T14:22:45.347Z","archivedAt":null,"completedAt":null,"startedAt":null,"canceledAt":null,"dueDate":null,"slaStartedAt":null,"slaMediumRiskAt":null,"slaHighRiskAt":null,"slaBreachesAt":null,"status":"Backlog","statusType":"backlog","labels":["area:providers","area:core","stage:3","Bug"],"attachments":[],"documents":[],"createdBy":"Sven Maschek","createdById":"ba6021cb-56c5-43aa-9797-fab3599d7ead","project":"Paigasus Helikon","projectId":"5d1fd72d-af2d-40f5-b562-fa04f8018610","team":"Sven Maschek","teamId":"7178572e-d61f-4cf0-bbcb-4e03c8d9f39e"}

{"id":"SMA-585","uuid":"e87dea71-f32a-4ffd-aafb-27e38eec8e87","title":"responses_tool_call.txt carries a trailing `data: [DONE]` its provenance header does not account for","description":"Surfaced by <issue id="1f92f811-7611-4138-aa57-b21d4dc5cc83" label="SMA-562" href="https://linear.app/smaschek/issue/SMA-562/openairesponses-reports-finishtoolcalls-for-a-function-call-that" /> while transcribing a new CAPTURED fixture into the same directory. Not a test failure — a provenance-accuracy gap in an artifact whose whole value is being trustworthy.

## The discrepancy

`crates/paigasus-helikon-providers-openai/tests/fixtures/responses_tool_call.txt` ends with:

```
data: [DONE]
```

Its provenance header states it is `CAPTURED against a real https://api.openai.com/v1/responses request, model gpt-4o-mini-2024-07-18 … on 2026-08-20`, and is explicit that

> a fixture claiming to be CAPTURED should stay faithful to what the wire actually sent, not just to what the parser happens to need.

It then enumerates **"Three kinds of trimming from the raw capture, all deliberate"** — dropped `response.created`/`response.in_progress`, dropped `obfuscation` fields, and a reduced `response` object (listing all 27 omitted keys by name). It is meticulous about removals and says nothing about the trailing `[DONE]`, because the header's structure has a slot for *trims* and none for *additions*.

## The evidence it may not have been sent

Four raw captures were taken on 2026-08-22 with `curl` against the same endpoint (`gpt-4o-mini`, `gpt-5-mini`, a `background: true` request, and a resumed stream). **None of the four contains** `[DONE]` — each ends on `response.completed` followed by a blank line.

That was verified rather than assumed: the byte-faithful capture was served through this directory's wiremock harness both as-is and with `data: [DONE]\n\n` appended, and the stream terminates **identically and cleanly either way** — async-openai ends the stream on body end, so the sentinel is not required by the parser. The new fixture `responses_tool_call_zero_args.txt` (added in <issue id="1f92f811-7611-4138-aa57-b21d4dc5cc83" label="SMA-562" href="https://linear.app/smaschek/issue/SMA-562/openairesponses-reports-finishtoolcalls-for-a-function-call-that" />) is therefore shipped byte-faithful with no sentinel, and its header flags this discrepancy as a follow-up.

Note the Chat Completions API *does* send `data: [DONE]` — the four `chat_*.txt` fixtures in the same directory are presumably correct. This is specifically about the Responses API.

## Two possible causes, and they need different fixes

1. **OpenAI sent it on 2026-08-20 and stopped by 2026-08-22.** Then the fixture is faithful to its capture date and only needs a header note pinning the observed behaviour to that date. This would also be worth knowing on its own.
2. **It was appended to match the sibling** `chat_*.txt` **fixtures**, and the trim-only header structure had nowhere to disclose an addition. Then the fixture is not byte-faithful and the `CAPTURED` label overstates it.

## Why this is worth a ticket rather than a shrug

Nothing breaks today. But this directory's fixtures are load-bearing: <issue id="9280dbb2-ab9c-4772-b566-0736392203ae" label="SMA-522" href="https://linear.app/smaschek/issue/SMA-522/openai-provider-emits-finish-before-usage-violating-the-core-event" />'s Gemini `FragmentedToolName` fixture went wrong precisely by being derived rather than captured, and this fixture's own header cites that incident as its reason for existing. A `CAPTURED` label that is even slightly overstated erodes the thing the label is for.

## Suggested resolution

* Re-capture a `get_weather`-style tool call against `/v1/responses` and settle empirically whether `[DONE]` is sent.
* Depending on the answer, either add a dated note to the header, or drop the line and record the removal.
* **Extend the provenance-header convention to cover additions as well as trims** — the current three-kinds-of-trimming structure cannot express "and one line was added", which is how this went unrecorded in the first place.
* While there: the same audit applies to the other `responses_*.txt` fixtures (`responses_reasoning_then_text.txt`, `responses_incomplete_length.txt`, `responses_incomplete_filter.txt`, `responses_failed.txt`), which all end in `[DONE]` too.

No production code is implicated — `ResponsesTranslator` handles both shapes correctly, which <issue id="1f92f811-7611-4138-aa57-b21d4dc5cc83" label="SMA-562" href="https://linear.app/smaschek/issue/SMA-562/openairesponses-reports-finishtoolcalls-for-a-function-call-that" /> verified.","priority":{"value":4,"name":"Low"},"url":"https://linear.app/smaschek/issue/SMA-585/responses-tool-calltxt-carries-a-trailing-data-done-its-provenance","gitBranchName":"feature/sma-585-responses_tool_calltxt-carries-a-trailing","createdAt":"2026-08-23T08:44:36.009Z","updatedAt":"2026-11-20T14:22:47.429Z","archivedAt":null,"completedAt":null,"startedAt":null,"canceledAt":null,"dueDate":null,"slaStartedAt":null,"slaMediumRiskAt":null,"slaHighRiskAt":null,"slaBreachesAt":null,"status":"Backlog","statusType":"backlog","labels":["area:providers","stage:3","Improvement"],"attachments":[],"documents":[],"createdBy":"Sven Maschek","createdById":"ba6021cb-56c5-43aa-9797-fab3599d7ead","project":"Paigasus Helikon","projectId":"5d1fd72d-af2d-40f5-b562-fa04f8018610","team":"Sven Maschek","teamId":"7178572e-d61f-4cf0-bbcb-4e03c8d9f39e"}

{"id":"SMA-567","uuid":"3aed9381-ac0f-4fb1-88cd-4344868ab0b3","title":"Extend the stream conformance suite to reasoning deltas, parallel tool calls and post-error events","description":"Coverage gaps recorded during <issue id="f3b29ed4-6162-4763-82d7-a529eab56e3e" label="SMA-533" href="https://linear.app/smaschek/issue/SMA-533/add-a-cross-provider-conformance-suite-for-stream-event-ordering" />, which deliberately scoped itself to the seven assertions in its own design doc.

## Not covered by the suite today

**1.** `ReasoningDelta` **ordering.** No scenario emits one. Anthropic (extended thinking), OpenAI (o-series/gpt-5) and Gemini all produce them, and their interleaving with `TokenDelta` is unasserted across every provider.

**2. Parallel tool calls.** Every tool scenario drives a single call. `ModelCapabilities` has a parallel-tool-call flag and `anthropic` ships a `parallel_tool_use.txt` fixture, so the shape is real and capturable. Assertion 7 is per-`call_id`, so multiple concurrent calls are exactly where a correlation bug would show.

**3. Events emitted after an** `Err`**.** `classify` guards what follows `Finish` but nothing constrains what follows an `Err`. A translator that keeps draining after an upstream error is unclassified by all five rules. Plausible from a broken translator; not in the design's assertion list.

**3b. A** `CleanStop` **adjacency floor.** The suite cannot currently detect a fixture whose terminal events are in an order the provider never sends. Recorded at `tests/provider-stream-conformance/tests/conformance.rs:176-186`: swapping bedrock's `metadata` and `messageStop` — a wire order Bedrock does not produce — was mutation-tested and **left the suite green**, because the translator handles both orders. The prose comment is the only guard today. A floor requiring `Usage` and `Finish` to be adjacent and terminal in `CleanStop` would close it for every subject at once, and would also re-cover the buffering path the translator exists for.

**4. Zero-argument tool calls.** Related to the Responses-backend defect filed separately — no scenario drives a tool call that streams no argument deltas.

## Note on how to add these

The suite's provenance rule is load-bearing: fixtures are transcribed from captured or already-committed traffic, never invented from vendor documentation. Two shapes in <issue id="f3b29ed4-6162-4763-82d7-a529eab56e3e" label="SMA-533" href="https://linear.app/smaschek/issue/SMA-533/add-a-cross-provider-conformance-suite-for-stream-event-ordering" /> had to be captured live rather than derived, and one derived shape was reverted in review for exactly this reason. Any new scenario needs a capture behind it.

## Acceptance criteria

* Each new assertion has a non-conformant fake proving it can fail, matching the existing `Fake` pattern.
* Each new scenario declares its declines in the pinned `DECLINED` table where a provider cannot express the shape.
* Every new fixture cites captured traffic.","priority":{"value":4,"name":"Low"},"url":"https://linear.app/smaschek/issue/SMA-567/extend-the-stream-conformance-suite-to-reasoning-deltas-parallel-tool","gitBranchName":"feature/sma-567-extend-the-stream-conformance-suite-to","createdAt":"2026-08-20T16:53:23.670Z","updatedAt":"2026-11-20T14:22:49.121Z","archivedAt":null,"completedAt":null,"startedAt":null,"canceledAt":null,"dueDate":null,"slaStartedAt":null,"slaMediumRiskAt":null,"slaHighRiskAt":null,"slaBreachesAt":null,"status":"Backlog","statusType":"backlog","labels":["area:providers","area:testing","stage:3","Improvement"],"attachments":[],"documents":[],"createdBy":"Sven Maschek","createdById":"ba6021cb-56c5-43aa-9797-fab3599d7ead","project":"Paigasus Helikon","projectId":"5d1fd72d-af2d-40f5-b562-fa04f8018610","team":"Sven Maschek","teamId":"7178572e-d61f-4cf0-bbcb-4e03c8d9f39e"}

{"id":"SMA-565","uuid":"03c8ce12-5202-49f7-a01d-3c0f6735ce75","title":"gemini live tests default to gemini-2.5-flash, which 404s for new API users","description":"Found while capturing a live Gemini tool-call stream for the <issue id="f3b29ed4-6162-4763-82d7-a529eab56e3e" label="SMA-533" href="https://linear.app/smaschek/issue/SMA-533/add-a-cross-provider-conformance-suite-for-stream-event-ordering" /> conformance suite on 2026-08-20.

## The defect

`crates/paigasus-helikon-providers-gemini/tests/live.rs:17` defaults `GEMINI_MODEL_ID` to `gemini-2.5-flash`. Against a Developer API key today that returns:

```
404 NOT_FOUND: This model models/gemini-2.5-flash is no longer available to new users.
Please update your code to use models/gemini-3.6-flash for the latest features and improvements.
```

`gemini-3.6-flash` works and was used for the capture.

## Why it is easy to miss

The live tests are env-gated and loud-skip without a credential, so CI never exercises this path. Anyone running them fresh gets a 404 that looks like a provider or auth problem rather than a stale default.

## Scope

Small. Bump the default and check whether the same model id appears elsewhere — the docs, the book, or other crates' examples.

## Acceptance criteria

* The default model id resolves for a new API key.

{"id":"SMA-564","uuid":"e0f06419-cb13-4432-916d-5df280eca094","title":"Unify the stream translator finish() return shape across the six providers","description":"Deferred out of <issue id="f3b29ed4-6162-4763-82d7-a529eab56e3e" label="SMA-533" href="https://linear.app/smaschek/issue/SMA-533/add-a-cross-provider-conformance-suite-for-stream-event-ordering" />. That ticket asked to "settle the `finish()` return shape"; the conformance suite it added asserts at the `Model::invoke` boundary and never observes `finish()`, so unifying it served no assertion there and would have mixed a five-crate signature refactor into a test-adding change.

## The divergence — four shapes, not the three the original ticket listed

| Subject | `consume` returns | `finish()` returns |
| -- | -- | -- |
| `openai/backend/chat` | `Vec<ModelEvent>` | `Vec<ModelEvent>` |
| `openai/backend/responses` | `Result<Vec<ModelEvent>, ModelError>` | *(absent)* |
| `anthropic` | `Result<Vec<Result<ModelEvent, ModelError>>, ModelError>` | `Option<Result<ModelEvent, ModelError>>` |
| `bedrock` | `Vec<Result<ModelEvent, ModelError>>` | `Option<Result<ModelEvent, ModelError>>` |
| `gemini` | `Vec<Result<ModelEvent, ModelError>>` | `Vec<Result<ModelEvent, ModelError>>` |
| `litellm` | `Vec<ModelEvent>` | `Vec<ModelEvent>` |

`openai/backend/responses` has **no** `finish()` **at all** — its `terminal_events` builds `Usage` and `Finish` together from one upstream event, and its driver is a bare `None => return` with no flush.

## Why it is safer to do now

The <issue id="f3b29ed4-6162-4763-82d7-a529eab56e3e" label="SMA-533" href="https://linear.app/smaschek/issue/SMA-533/add-a-cross-provider-conformance-suite-for-stream-event-ordering" /> suite exercises all six drivers end to end at the HTTP boundary, including truncation, cancellation and mid-stream error paths. A refactor of the flush signatures is now guarded by tests that did not exist when the divergence was flagged.

## Note

Any candidate design has to account for `responses` genuinely not needing a flush, rather than adding an empty one for symmetry.

## Acceptance criteria

* One shape across all six, or a documented rationale at each site that keeps a different one.
* The conformance suite stays green throughout, and no provider's observable event sequence changes.","priority":{"value":4,"name":"Low"},"url":"https://linear.app/smaschek/issue/SMA-564/unify-the-stream-translator-finish-return-shape-across-the-six","gitBranchName":"feature/sma-564-unify-the-stream-translator-finish-return","createdAt":"2026-08-20T16:52:51.235Z","updatedAt":"2026-11-20T14:22:53.395Z","archivedAt":null,"completedAt":null,"startedAt":null,"canceledAt":null,"dueDate":null,"slaStartedAt":null,"slaMediumRiskAt":null,"slaHighRiskAt":null,"slaBreachesAt":null,"status":"Backlog","statusType":"backlog","labels":["area:providers","stage:3","Improvement"],"attachments":[],"documents":[],"createdBy":"Sven Maschek","createdById":"ba6021cb-56c5-43aa-9797-fab3599d7ead","project":"Paigasus Helikon","projectId":"5d1fd72d-af2d-40f5-b562-fa04f8018610","team":"Sven Maschek","teamId":"7178572e-d61f-4cf0-bbcb-4e03c8d9f39e"}

{"id":"SMA-548","uuid":"cdfeac84-4b41-43b2-bb34-2c35f0d3ef6b","title":"Anthropic finish_or_error: three stop-reason mappings have no assertion on either emission path","description":"Found by the final whole-branch review of PR #200. Pre-existing gap — that PR neither created nor widened it.

## The gap

`crates/paigasus-helikon-providers-anthropic/src/stream.rs`'s `finish_or_error` maps a wire `stop_reason` string to a terminal event:

| `stop_reason` | Result | Asserted anywhere? |
| -- | -- | -- |
| `end_turn` | `Finish{Stop}` | yes |
| `stop_sequence` | `Finish{Stop}` | **no** |
| `max_tokens` | `Finish{Length}` | **no** |
| `tool_use` | `Finish{ToolCalls}` / `Finish{Stop}` / `Err(Other)` | yes |
| `refusal` | `Err(Refused)` | yes |
| *anything else* | `Finish{Other(reason)}` | **no** |

Three rows have no assertion **anywhere in the crate, on either emission path** — neither the inline `message_stop` path nor the `finish()` clean-EOF path added in PR #200. The one place `max_tokens` appears in a test (`second_message_delta_after_message_stop_does_not_double_finish`) asserts `finish().is_none()`, so control never reaches the mapper.

## Why it is worth closing

`FinishReason::Length` is the signal a consumer needs to distinguish "the model finished" from "the model was cut off by the token budget" — arguably the most consequential mapping in the table after `ToolCalls`, and the only one with no test at all.

The `other` fallback is the forward-compatibility path: if Anthropic ships a new stop reason, that branch is what runs, and nothing pins its shape. Note `sse.rs`'s `AnthropicEvent` has no catch-all variant either, so unknown *event* types already fail deserialization and are skipped — the unknown *stop reason* path is the one that stays live.

## Scope

Small. Both emission sites share `finish_or_error`, so plain inline unit tests in `stream.rs`'s existing `mod tests` suffice — no new fixtures, no integration tests, no production change. Three tests, one per unasserted row.

## Not a duplicate

Distinct from the cross-provider stream event-ordering conformance suite, which is about *ordering* across providers. This is one crate's reason-mapping table having untested rows.","priority":{"value":4,"name":"Low"},"url":"https://linear.app/smaschek/issue/SMA-548/anthropic-finish-or-error-three-stop-reason-mappings-have-no-assertion","gitBranchName":"feature/sma-548-anthropic-finish_or_error-three-stop-reason","createdAt":"2026-08-17T19:54:04.147Z","updatedAt":"2026-11-20T14:22:55.592Z","archivedAt":null,"completedAt":null,"startedAt":null,"canceledAt":null,"dueDate":null,"slaStartedAt":null,"slaMediumRiskAt":null,"slaHighRiskAt":null,"slaBreachesAt":null,"status":"Backlog","statusType":"backlog","labels":["area:providers","area:testing","stage:3","Improvement"],"attachments":[],"documents":[],"createdBy":"Sven Maschek","createdById":"ba6021cb-56c5-43aa-9797-fab3599d7ead","project":"Paigasus Helikon","projectId":"5d1fd72d-af2d-40f5-b562-fa04f8018610","team":"Sven Maschek","teamId":"7178572e-d61f-4cf0-bbcb-4e03c8d9f39e"}

{"id":"SMA-544","uuid":"0081979a-baa1-419d-a201-f480358cf9a2","title":"litellm provider hardening: redact_endpoint residual, test env races, secret-header table drift","description":"Three residuals adjudicated and parked during PR #199 (<issue id="3ff83fb5-f03b-4518-920a-a7ba0ec8d3e8" label="SMA-451" href="https://linear.app/smaschek/issue/SMA-451/provider-crate-paigasus-helikon-providers-litellm" />). None were load-bearing enough to block that PR; all are small.

## 1. `redact_endpoint` does not redact a cannot-be-a-base URL (the one with security flavour)

`crates/paigasus-helikon-providers-litellm/src/builder.rs` — `redact_endpoint` blanks userinfo via `Url::set_username` / `set_password`, but both return `Err(())` for a cannot-be-a-base URL and the results are discarded, so `to_string()` returns the input verbatim.

Reachable through the `BuildError::InvalidBaseUrl` path that PR #199 added redaction to:

```
base_url("admin:s3cret@gw:4000")
```

That is a scheme-less paste of exactly the basic-auth-fronted shape the redactor exists for. It parses with scheme `admin`, fails `normalise_endpoint`'s scheme check, and renders as `invalid base URL: admin:s3cret@gw:4000` — password intact, into whatever the caller logs.

The crate's own `transport.rs` calls the scheme-less form "the single most likely operator typo", so the case is not exotic.

**Blast radius is narrow**: build-time error only, scheme-less URL only, inline credentials only.

**Suggested fix**: stop echoing the input at all on a parse-class failure, rather than extending the redactor to handle a shape `Url` cannot manipulate. That is a small behaviour change to `BuildError::InvalidBaseUrl`'s payload and should be made deliberately rather than folded into an unrelated PR.

## 2. Four `build()`-without-`.api_key()` sites race the env tests

`crates/paigasus-helikon-providers-litellm/tests/litellm_wire.rs` (2 sites, added by PR #199's final fix wave) and `src/model.rs` (2 pre-existing sites) call `build()` without `.api_key()`, so each performs a `getenv("LITELLM_API_KEY")` inside `non_empty_env` concurrently with `builder.rs`'s nine env tests calling `std::env::set_var` / `remove_var` under a lock these sites do not take. Same test binary, multi-threaded harness — a genuine getenv/setenv data race.

Benign today (none of the four assert anything about auth), but race-induced test crashes are among the hardest CI flakes to diagnose after the fact. PR #199 closed the same class in `translate/mod.rs`; these were out of that fix's scope.

**Fix**: add `.api_key("sk-test")` to each — one line per site.

## 3. The secret-header redaction test table is hand-copied

`crates/paigasus-helikon-providers-litellm/src/builder.rs` — the table-driven redaction test added by PR #199 iterates a literal list rather than deriving from `is_secret_header`. It catches **deletion** of an entry (the failure mode it was added for) but not a future entry **added** to the predicate and not to the table.

**Fix**: extract a `const SECRET_HEADER_EXACT: &[&str]` consumed by both the predicate and the test, so drift is impossible.","priority":{"value":4,"name":"Low"},"url":"https://linear.app/smaschek/issue/SMA-544/litellm-provider-hardening-redact-endpoint-residual-test-env-races","gitBranchName":"feature/sma-544-litellm-provider-hardening-redact_endpoint","createdAt":"2026-08-16T20:32:16.959Z","updatedAt":"2026-11-20T14:22:57.629Z","archivedAt":null,"completedAt":null,"startedAt":null,"canceledAt":null,"dueDate":null,"slaStartedAt":null,"slaMediumRiskAt":null,"slaHighRiskAt":null,"slaBreachesAt":null,"status":"Backlog","statusType":"backlog","labels":["area:providers","area:testing","stage:3","Improvement"],"attachments":[],"documents":[],"createdBy":"Sven Maschek","createdById":"ba6021cb-56c5-43aa-9797-fab3599d7ead","project":"Paigasus Helikon","projectId":"5d1fd72d-af2d-40f5-b562-fa04f8018610","team":"Sven Maschek","teamId":"7178572e-d61f-4cf0-bbcb-4e03c8d9f39e"}

{"id":"SMA-532","uuid":"3df9eaf8-0843-427c-a9bd-c46b8404f820","title":"Bedrock stream.rs doc comments misstate the core Usage/Finish ordering contract","description":"Documentation-only. The Bedrock code is correct; its prose is not.

## The defect

`crates/paigasus-helikon-providers-bedrock/src/stream.rs:14` and `:439` both assert that `ModelEvent::Usage` **must precede** `ModelEvent::Finish` "per the ordering contract".

The core contract (`crates/paigasus-helikon-core/src/model.rs:55-63`) says no such thing:

> * `Usage` MAY appear anywhere; most providers emit one immediately before `Finish` \[…\]
> * `Finish` is the terminal event; nothing follows it.

Only `Finish` is positionally constrained. `Usage` is not.

## Why it is worth fixing

This exact misreading is the **root cause** of the OpenAI defect fixed in PR #197 — it made emitting `Finish` inline look correct, because the author believed the contract was about `Usage`'s position rather than `Finish`'s terminality. The same sentence surviving verbatim in a sibling provider is a live trap for the next person who reads it.

The OpenAI and Responses instances were corrected in PR #197; these two were deferred to keep that PR scoped to one crate.

## Scope

Comment text only, at both sites. No behaviour change. {"id":"SMA-523","uuid":"6de26da5-84af-47dc-b89c-2c12ee5cd6fd","title":"Add a signal-only litellm-it CI job using a keyless LiteLLM container","description":"Follow-up from <issue id="3ff83fb5-f03b-4518-920a-a7ba0ec8d3e8" label="SMA-451" href="https://linear.app/smaschek/issue/SMA-451/provider-crate-paigasus-helikon-providers-litellm" />. Blocked by <issue id="3ff83fb5-f03b-4518-920a-a7ba0ec8d3e8" label="SMA-451" href="https://linear.app/smaschek/issue/SMA-451/provider-crate-paigasus-helikon-providers-litellm" /> landing (the crate and its `tests/live.rs` must exist first).

## Why

<issue id="3ff83fb5-f03b-4518-920a-a7ba0ec8d3e8" label="SMA-451" href="https://linear.app/smaschek/issue/SMA-451/provider-crate-paigasus-helikon-providers-litellm" />'s design initially asserted that a live LiteLLM CI job "needs a container plus at least one real upstream key", so it could never be more than a loud-skip. **That premise is false and was retracted.**

LiteLLM's `mock_response` deployments serve full streaming SSE, real router fallbacks, and real LiteLLM error envelopes with `api_key: fake-key`. The entire verification rig behind <issue id="3ff83fb5-f03b-4518-920a-a7ba0ec8d3e8" label="SMA-451" href="https://linear.app/smaschek/issue/SMA-451/provider-crate-paigasus-helikon-providers-litellm" />'s Appendix B ran **without any upstream credential**.

This matters because that rig caught two defects that both a careful design pass and an adversarial spec review had missed:

1. `usage` arrives in a **separate trailing chunk after** the `finish_reason` chunk — the design would have violated core's `Finish`-is-terminal contract on every turn. (Also a live bug in the OpenAI provider — <issue id="9280dbb2-ab9c-4772-b566-0736392203ae" label="SMA-522" href="https://linear.app/smaschek/issue/SMA-522/openai-provider-emits-finish-before-usage-violating-the-core-event" />.)
2. `error.code` is the **HTTP status as a string** (`"400"`, `"429"`, `"500"`), not a semantic code — so the designed primary classification signal could never have matched anything.

Both are wire-shape facts that only real traffic reveals. Wiremock tests assert what we *think* the wire looks like; this job would assert what it *is*.

## Scope

Add a `litellm-it` job to `.github/workflows/integration.yml`, following the `temporal-it` pattern already established there:

* **Signal-only**: not listed in `.github/rulesets/main-protection-checks.json`. Signal-only means *not required*, never `continue-on-error` — that would report green unconditionally and destroy the signal.
* **Step-level** `if:` **guards, not job-level.** A skipped job reports no status at all, which blocks every PR the moment the context is promoted. Same reasoning as `sessions-it`.
* Boot `ghcr.io/berriai/litellm:main-stable` (pin the digest; nothing tracks this automatically — it joins `TEMPORAL_CLI_VERSION` and `NIGHTLY_TOOLCHAIN` as a hand-bumped pin) with a `mock_response` config, and probe readiness on `/health/liveliness`.
* Run `tests/live.rs` with an env var that turns its loud-skip into a **panic**, mirroring `HELIKON_REQUIRE_TEMPORAL` / `HELIKON_REQUIRE_SANDBOX`. Without it a job that never reached the proxy is indistinguishable from a green one, because a skipped test passes and `cargo test` captures its output.
* Reuse the config in Appendix B of `docs/superpowers/specs/2026-08-16-sma-451-litellm-provider-design.md`.

## What this can and cannot cover

**Can**: streaming chunk ordering and shape, usage field presence, error envelope structure and status codes, `fallbacks`/`num_retries`/`metadata.tags` acceptance and routing, URL/auth handling, `x-litellm-*` response headers.

**Cannot**: anything requiring a real backend — streaming tool-call `index` presence, reasoning-field naming (`reasoning_content` vs `reasoning` vs `thinking_blocks`), and true mid-stream error frames. These are listed as open unknowns in <issue id="3ff83fb5-f03b-4518-920a-a7ba0ec8d3e8" label="SMA-451" href="https://linear.app/smaschek/issue/SMA-451/provider-crate-paigasus-helikon-providers-litellm" /> §17 and stay open.

## Promotion

Same bar as `temporal-it`: ≥ 20 executed runs with ≤ 1 flake, or 30 consecutive green nightlies, before adding it to `main-protection-checks.json` and CONTRIBUTING.md's required-contexts table.","priority":{"value":4,"name":"Low"},"url":"https://linear.app/smaschek/issue/SMA-523/add-a-signal-only-litellm-it-ci-job-using-a-keyless-litellm-container","gitBranchName":"feature/sma-523-add-a-signal-only-litellm-it-ci-job-using-a","createdAt":"2026-08-16T08:19:19.182Z","updatedAt":"2026-11-20T14:23:02.365Z","archivedAt":null,"completedAt":null,"startedAt":null,"canceledAt":null,"dueDate":null,"slaStartedAt":null,"slaMediumRiskAt":null,"slaHighRiskAt":null,"slaBreachesAt":null,"status":"Backlog","statusType":"backlog","labels":["area:providers","area:testing","area:ci","stage:3","Improvement"],"attachments":[],"documents":[],"createdBy":"Sven Maschek","createdById":"ba6021cb-56c5-43aa-9797-fab3599d7ead","project":"Paigasus Helikon","projectId":"5d1fd72d-af2d-40f5-b562-fa04f8018610","team":"Sven Maschek","teamId":"7178572e-d61f-4cf0-bbcb-4e03c8d9f39e"}

{"id":"SMA-450","uuid":"cf30634a-eeb6-4342-b90c-c40b0374858a","title":"Provider crate: paigasus-helikon-providers-ollama","description":"Split from <issue id="6348b8a6-ebb0-483d-a452-a3ca54d99a8a" label="SMA-329" href="https://linear.app/smaschek/issue/SMA-329/additional-providers-bedrock-gemini-ollama-litellm" /> (which now delivers the Bedrock provider; see that issue for the decision). Follows the brand-new-crate pattern established by `paigasus-helikon-providers-bedrock`.

## Scope

`paigasus-helikon-providers-ollama` — local Ollama provider (HTTP against the local Ollama daemon, or `ollama-rs`; pick during brainstorming). New self-contained crate behind an `ollama` Cargo feature on the facade. Targets the local/offline dev story.

## Acceptance criteria

* Implements `paigasus_helikon_core::Model` with the same public surface shape as the OpenAI/Anthropic providers (`OllamaModel` + builder).
* Passes the same wire-format snapshot suite the OpenAI/Anthropic providers do.
* New crate is name-claimed on [crates.io](<http://crates.io>) and wired into the facade (optional dep + `ollama` feature), mirroring the Bedrock crate from <issue id="6348b8a6-ebb0-483d-a452-a3ca54d99a8a" label="SMA-329" href="https://linear.app/smaschek/issue/SMA-329/additional-providers-bedrock-gemini-ollama-litellm" />.

<issue id="d38f7a37-3691-4df7-939f-8a2d7b7df257" label="SMA-779" href="https://linear.app/smaschek/issue/SMA-779/ignore-rustsec-2026-0543-chrono-unmaintained-until-upstream-crates" /> (PR #341) added `RUSTSEC-2026-0543` ("chrono is unmaintained") to the ignore lists in `deny.toml` and `.cargo/audit.toml`. The workspace does not depend on chrono directly. Six upstream crates pull it in, and no dependency update removes it today.

This ticket tracks the removal of that ignore entry.

## Upstream status (2026-11-17)

| Upstream crate | Our crate | Tracking |
| -- | -- | -- |
| rmcp 3.x (also enables `schemars/chrono04`) | mcp | [rust-sdk#1469](<https://github.com/modelcontextprotocol/rust-sdk/issues/1469>), open, no maintainer reply yet |
| arrow / parquet 60.x | evals | [arrow-rs#9183](<https://github.com/apache/arrow-rs/issues/9183>), open, migration to jiff accepted, multi-step and breaking |
| gcp_auth 0.12 | providers | none |
| prost-wkt 0.7 | runtime-temporal | none |
| temporalio-common-wasm 1.0 | runtime-temporal | none |
| schemars 1.x | core | not needed: chrono is optional (`chrono04`), only rmcp turns it on |

## When to act

Check again on each bump of rmcp, arrow/parquet, gcp_auth, prost-wkt or temporalio-\*. Check the two upstream issues above for progress.

## Steps

1. Confirm that `cargo tree --all-features -i chrono` shows no result.
2. Remove the `RUSTSEC-2026-0543` entry and its comment from `deny.toml` and `.cargo/audit.toml`.
3. Run `cargo audit --deny warnings` and `cargo deny --all-features check`. Both must pass.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] chrono is not in `Cargo.lock`.
- [ ] `RUSTSEC-2026-0543` is not in `deny.toml` or `.cargo/audit.toml`.
- [ ] The `audit` and `deny` gates pass on the PR and on `main`.

## Partial progress

If only some upstream crates drop chrono, update the table above. {"id":"SMA-746","uuid":"e7f12995-495f-43f9-bf43-9225c2cdefaa","title":"ci(release): move the three release secrets into the release environment","description":"PR #320 gave the paigasusbot App token `workflows: write` and moved the `release-plz` job into the `release` environment, which only `main` can deploy to. The secrets did not move yet. They are still **repository** secrets, so a workflow on any branch can read them.

Status on 2026-11-01:

* The `release` environment exists with exactly one branch policy, `main`.
* `gh secret list --env release` is empty.
* The repository secrets `RELEASE_PLZ_APP_CLIENT_ID`, `RELEASE_PLZ_APP_PRIVATE_KEY` and `CARGO_REGISTRY_TOKEN` are still in place. The job reads them through the environment, so the releases work.

GitHub never shows a secret value again, so the values cannot be copied. Enter them again:

1. `RELEASE_PLZ_APP_CLIENT_ID`: copy it from the paigasusbot App settings. It is not secret.
2. `RELEASE_PLZ_APP_PRIVATE_KEY`: make a new private key in the App settings.
3. `CARGO_REGISTRY_TOKEN`: make a new token on [crates.io](<http://crates.io>).
4. Set each one with `gh secret set <NAME> --env release` (the command asks for the value, so it does not go into the shell history).
5. Check them with `gh secret list --env release`.
6. After the next good `release-plz` run, delete the three repository secrets. Then revoke the old App key and the old [crates.io](<http://crates.io>) token.

Runbook: `docs/runbooks/release-ascend.md`, the <issue id="adcaf88e-16f9-4d19-8b0a-1e921f9bdb6c" label="SMA-745" href="https://linear.app/smaschek/issue/SMA-745/release-plz-post-gitrefs-returns-403-when-a-workflow-changing-pr" /> section, "Rollout".

## Acceptance criteria

* `gh secret list --env release` lists the three secrets.
* `gh secret list` (repository level) does not list them.
* A `release-plz` run after the change is green, and its "report release gaps" step says "no gaps".","priority":{"value":2,"name":"High"},"url":"https://linear.app/smaschek/issue/SMA-746/cirelease-move-the-three-release-secrets-into-the-release-environment","gitBranchName":"feature/sma-746-cirelease-move-the-three-release-secrets","createdAt":"2026-11-01T20:13:02.929Z","updatedAt":"2026-11-20T14:23:09.643Z","archivedAt":null,"completedAt":null,"startedAt":null,"canceledAt":null,"dueDate":null,"slaStartedAt":null,"slaMediumRiskAt":null,"slaHighRiskAt":null,"slaBreachesAt":null,"status":"Backlog","statusType":"backlog","labels":["area:release","area:ci","stage:3","Improvement"],"attachments":[],"documents":[],"createdBy":"Sven Maschek","createdById":"ba6021cb-56c5-43aa-9797-fab3599d7ead","project":"Paigasus Helikon","projectId":"5d1fd72d-af2d-40f5-b562-fa04f8018610","team":"Sven Maschek","teamId":"7178572e-d61f-4cf0-bbcb-4e03c8d9f39e"}

{"id":"SMA-545","uuid":"9428dc2f-7922-40d3-984f-77875fa6eadb","title":"Sweep remaining stale facade version pins and provider lists in the mdBook","description":"Confirmed pre-existing during PR #199 (<issue id="3ff83fb5-f03b-4518-920a-a7ba0ec8d3e8" label="SMA-451" href="https://linear.app/smaschek/issue/SMA-451/provider-crate-paigasus-helikon-providers-litellm" />) and deliberately left out of that PR's scope.

## Stale facade version pins

PR #199 bumped the whole `0.3` → `0.5` block in `docs/book/src/concepts/model-providers.md` (it had to, because the newly added `litellm` line inherited the stale pin and `0.3.x` has no `litellm` feature). Two sites were out of scope and are now the last stale facade pins in the book:

* `docs/book/src/getting-started/quickstart.md:9` — pins `version = "0.3"`
* `docs/book/src/getting-started/workspace-layout.md:91` — pins `version = "0.4"`

The facade is currently `0.5.5`. Both snippets are copy-pasteable and wrong.

(`model-providers.md`'s `providers-gemini = "0.1"` is accurate against gemini `0.1.5` — no action there.)

Consider whether these snippets should carry versions at all: the crate READMEs deliberately use `cargo add` with no hardcoded version precisely so a routine release needs no doc edit. Applying the same convention to the book would stop this recurring.

## Incomplete provider / feature enumerations

Also confirmed pre-existing, unrelated to litellm:

* `docs/book/src/introduction.md` — the "Providers" bullet names only `openai` and `anthropic`, omitting bedrock, gemini and now litellm.
* `docs/book/src/getting-started/workspace-layout.md` — the feature table is missing rows for `bedrock`, `gemini`, `sessions-postgres`, `sessions-redis`, `runtime-actix` and `litellm`.

## Why this keeps happening

Several book pages carry a hardcoded provider or crate count in prose ("Four adapters ship today", "Twenty crates are published"). PR #199 had to update **seven** such figures across five files, five of which were not on the original checklist and were only found by grepping. Each is a silent staleness trap.

Worth considering as part of this sweep: either drop the counts in favour of phrasing that does not need maintenance, or add a docs test / CI check that asserts the enumerations match the actual `crates/` listing and the facade's `[features]` table. The latter is what would actually stop the drift — this is the same class of problem <issue id="74d39715-d394-4612-b82a-8f86059068f9" label="SMA-423" href="https://linear.app/smaschek/issue/SMA-423/refresh-the-public-mdbook-to-reflect-shipped-surface-book-is-still-the" /> was the one-time catch-up for.","priority":{"value":4,"name":"Low"},"url":"https://linear.app/smaschek/issue/SMA-545/sweep-remaining-stale-facade-version-pins-and-provider-lists-in-the","gitBranchName":"feature/sma-545-sweep-remaining-stale-facade-version-pins","createdAt":"2026-08-16T20:32:36.546Z","updatedAt":"2026-11-20T14:23:11.899Z","archivedAt":null,"completedAt":null,"startedAt":null,"canceledAt":null,"dueDate":null,"slaStartedAt":null,"slaMediumRiskAt":null,"slaHighRiskAt":null,"slaBreachesAt":null,"status":"Backlog","statusType":"backlog","labels":["area:docs","stage:3","Improvement"],"attachments":[],"documents":[],"createdBy":"Sven Maschek","createdById":"ba6021cb-56c5-43aa-9797-fab3599d7ead","project":"Paigasus Helikon","projectId":"5d1fd72d-af2d-40f5-b562-fa04f8018610","team":"Sven Maschek","teamId":"7178572e-d61f-4cf0-bbcb-4e03c8d9f39e"}

{"id":"SMA-816","uuid":"18ce9d27-aa5c-47a8-b642-c0e2e994f3ec","title":"Add a SessionEvent::ToolDeferred conformance test to the sessions testkit","description":"## Goal

The published sessions testkit checks that a `Session` backend stores and returns `SessionEvent::ToolDeferred` correctly. An external backend such as `PgRunSession` then gets this check from the suite (ADR-0028, decision (b)).

This is the second part of <issue id="d7663b3e-83bc-4f55-bb55-3295ea282237" label="SMA-805" href="https://linear.app/smaschek/issue/SMA-805/publish-paigasus-helikon-sessions-testkit-to-cratesio" />. <issue id="d7663b3e-83bc-4f55-bb55-3295ea282237" label="SMA-805" href="https://linear.app/smaschek/issue/SMA-805/publish-paigasus-helikon-sessions-testkit-to-cratesio" /> (PR <pull-request id="bad74285-915b-4b70-a5da-2f301d98ed85" label="SMK1085/paigasus-helikon#343" href="https://linear.app/smaschek/review/choresessions-sma-805-publish-the-sessions-testkit-to-cratesio-733074a0f227" />) publishes the existing suite at `0.1.0`. This issue adds the `ToolDeferred` test after <issue id="843747f9-8bd2-46a1-b9cf-e47aefa21a5a" label="SMA-803" href="https://linear.app/smaschek/issue/SMA-803/deferred-tool-calls-a-defer-decision-ends-the-run-at-the-turn-boundary" /> merges.

## Scope

- [ ] Add a sub-test, for example `run_tool_deferred`, and call it from `run_all`.
- [ ] Append a `ToolDeferred` event, read it back, and compare the `serde_json::Value` forms. `SessionEvent` has no `PartialEq`. Use whole-second timestamps.
- [ ] Check that `project()` adds no `Item` for the event.
- [ ] Check the open-deferral rule with `open_deferrals(events)`: a `ToolDeferred` with no later `ToolReturned` for the same `call_id` is open. A later `ToolReturned` closes it.
- [ ] Run the new test against every built-in backend: memory, SQLite, Postgres, Redis and the compacting wrapper.
- [ ] Update the testkit README, the crate rustdoc and `docs/book/src/concepts/sessions.md` with the new sub-test.

## Done when

* The testkit release that contains this test is on [crates.io](<http://crates.io>). It must build against the core version that has `ToolDeferred`.
* The <issue id="d7663b3e-83bc-4f55-bb55-3295ea282237" label="SMA-805" href="https://linear.app/smaschek/issue/SMA-805/publish-paigasus-helikon-sessions-testkit-to-cratesio" /> "Done when" is met: the testkit version on [crates.io](<http://crates.io>) includes the deferred-tool-calls change.

## Release notes

* The test uses core API that <issue id="843747f9-8bd2-46a1-b9cf-e47aefa21a5a" label="SMA-803" href="https://linear.app/smaschek/issue/SMA-803/deferred-tool-calls-a-defer-decision-ends-the-run-at-the-turn-boundary" /> adds. If the core release that has `ToolDeferred` is not on [crates.io](<http://crates.io>) yet, this PR must also bump core. `cargo publish --verify` builds against the registry core (see `docs/runbooks/release-ascend.md`).

{"id":"SMA-763","uuid":"ca826652-1713-4b1a-851e-f0abb9fe2308","title":"Ignore RUSTSEC-2026-0459 (libsqlite3-sys 0.37) until sqlx allows libsqlite3-sys >= 0.39","description":"## What happened

On 2026-11-12, the `audit` and `deny` gates on `main` failed. The cause is a new advisory, RUSTSEC-2026-0459. It flags `libsqlite3-sys` 0.37.0, which bundles C SQLite with CVE-2026-119375 (severity 6.8, medium). The fix is `libsqlite3-sys` 0.39.0 or later.

The failure is not from a code change. The async-openai bump, [https://github.com/SMK1085/paigasus-helikon/pull/331](<https://github.com/SMK1085/paigasus-helikon/pull/331>), was the first push to `main` after the advisory was published.

## Why a lockfile update cannot fix it

`sqlx-sqlite` 0.9.0 requires `libsqlite3-sys = ">=0.30.1, <0.38.0"`. `sqlx` 0.9.0 is the latest release. Thus no compatible fixed version exists.

Path: `libsqlite3-sys` → `sqlx-sqlite` → `sqlx` → `paigasus-helikon-evals`, `paigasus-helikon-sessions-sqlite`, `paigasus-helikon-sessions-postgres`.

## Upstream status (checked 2026-11-12)

* [crates.io](<http://crates.io>): `sqlx` and `sqlx-sqlite` max version is 0.9.0. No newer release or pre-release exists.
* Upstream fix: [https://github.com/launchbadge/sqlx/pull/4502](<https://github.com/launchbadge/sqlx/pull/4502>) ("Bump the upper bound on libsqlite3-sys to allow 0.39.x") merged on 2026-11-08. `sqlx-sqlite` on upstream `main` requires `>=0.30.1, <0.40.0`. The change is not in a release yet.
* We did not use a `[patch.crates-io]` git dependency. It changes only our lockfile, not what users of the published crates resolve.

## Decision

Sven decided on 2026-11-12: add RUSTSEC-2026-0459 to the ignore lists in `.cargo/audit.toml` and `deny.toml`. This unblocks all PRs. This ticket tracks the removal of the ignore.

## To do

- [X] Add the ignore to `.cargo/audit.toml` and `deny.toml`.
- [ ] When a `sqlx` release allows `libsqlite3-sys` >= 0.39, bump `sqlx` and remove both ignore entries.
- [ ] Make sure that `cargo audit --deny warnings` and `cargo deny check advisories` pass without the ignore.

## Note

The vulnerable SQLite code ships in the published crates that use `sqlx` with SQLite. {"id":"SMA-810","uuid":"25885f3b-a366-4df6-bb75-6e2683c4b0ab","title":"Handoff transfer call has no tool result, so the stored session gets a late synthetic ToolReturned","description":"## Problem

In a run with a handoff, the transfer tool call never gets a tool result in the event stream. `transition()` emits a `ToolCallItem` for the transfer call, but no `ToolOutputItem` (`crates/paigasus-helikon-core/src/loop_state.rs:298-302`).

`SessionRecorder::drain` then adds a synthetic `ToolReturned` for this orphan call. It adds the result at the **end** of the log, after all the events of the handoff child (`crates/paigasus-helikon-core/src/session.rs:541-543`).

## Why it matters

When the session is sent to a model again, the transfer `ToolCall` and its result are far apart. Some providers require the result directly after the call, and they can reject the request.

This behaviour already exists. The <issue id="61ccebe8-5359-478a-8741-d101146a03cb" label="SMA-804" href="https://linear.app/smaschek/issue/SMA-804/turn-boundary-checkpoint-a-runcontext-callback-that-can-continue" /> spec challenge found it.

## Done when

* The stored session of a handoff run has the result of the transfer call directly after the call.
* A test checks that every `ToolCalled` in a handoff run has its `ToolReturned` next to it.

>>> Agent notes

* Found by the adversarial spec challenge for <issue id="61ccebe8-5359-478a-8741-d101146a03cb" label="SMA-804" href="https://linear.app/smaschek/issue/SMA-804/turn-boundary-checkpoint-a-runcontext-callback-that-can-continue" /> (spec `docs/superpowers/specs/2026-11-18-sma-804-turn-boundary-checkpoint-design.md`, section 5.5).
* A possible fix is that `transition()` emits a `ToolOutputItem` for the transfer call (for example "transferred to <agent>") before the handoff. Check the provider wire order for handoff transcripts (`thread_handoff_transcript`) first.

lastPrompt: Check the linear project, make sure all issues under Helikon are properly tagged, have the correct priority and if any ticket blocks another has that reflected in linear

content.text:
I updated all 20 open issues in the "Paigasus Helikon" project (17 Backlog, 3 In Progress, none in Triage). Each change shows in the response from Linear.

**Labels.** Each open issue now has at least one `area:*` label, one `stage:*` label, and one type label (Bug, Feature or Improvement).
- SMA-819 and SMA-820 had no labels. Each now has `area:providers`, `stage:3` and `Bug`.
- Some issues had no labels or only an `area:*` label. They got the missing stage and type labels, plus extra area labels where the description supports them: `area:testing` on 548, 544, 565, 567, 523 and 816; `area:core` on 621; `area:docs` on 532; `area:ci` on 523, 746, 763 and 782.
- SMA-450 got `Feature`. SMA-810 got `stage:3` and `Bug`.

**Priority.**
- SMA-819 went from no priority to **High**. The Anthropic API probably rejects an empty text block with HTTP 400, and each replay of the session fails again.
- SMA-820 went from no priority to **Medium**. Nobody has confirmed that the Gemini API rejects two adjacent user contents, and only two paths produce that shape.
- All other priorities did not change, because I found no clear reason to change them.

**Blocking relations.** I added no new relations, because I found no open issue that blocks another open issue. Each blocker named in a description is already Done: SMA-451 for SMA-523, SMA-533 for 564/567, and SMA-803/805 for SMA-816. SMA-816 already has its blocked-by relation to SMA-803. SMA-763 and SMA-782 wait only for upstream releases (sqlx, rmcp, arrow-rs and others), and Linear cannot show those as blockers.

**Choices you can reverse:**
1. I gave `stage:3` to the CI, release and deps issues (746, 763, 782), not `stage:0`. SMA-805 has `stage:3`, and all current work is in Stage 3. Tell me if you prefer `stage:0`.
2. SMA-763 is In Progress, but the ignore is already in place (PR #334). The remaining steps wait for a sqlx release. It can probably go back to Backlog. I did not change its status.

**Not done:** I did not change any Done issues. Many of them have no labels, for example SMA-817, SMA-818, SMA-780, SMA-779 and most of the SMA-6xx/7xx CI issues. I can re-label those too if you want.
